utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I just wanted to state it for the record that my colleague has been injured -- and my client in fact has an injury, and he's agreed for us to continue our work in his absence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we are grateful for that, Mr. Aleksic. I hope he recovers quickly and is back with us as soon as possible. Good morning, Ms. Xhafa.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will continue with your evidence. I have to remind you, though, first of all, that the solemn declaration which you took at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Xhafa.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, I will now ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like the witness to be shown Defence Exhibit 3D66.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I would like you to show on this map the location where you stopped, in fact where you were while the convoy was not in motion. But first of all, I would like to ask you, you said that you found Fazil and Musa again there, you encountered them here again. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Who's Musa?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fazil and Mirsad.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, Fazil and Mirsad, we met them on the way somewhere in lower Studime.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you remember at what time it happened, what time it was, approximately? Or let me assist you in a different way. Was it before the convoy stopped?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was the time when we were on our way to Vushtrri, after the massacre. We were ordered to go to Vushtrri, and it was somewhere on -- at Studime i Ulet, or lower Studime, that we met Fazil and Mirsad.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show the Defence Exhibit D -- I'm sorry, 3D66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you have it on the screen, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, this is a map similar to the one you used yesterday, but this time it is in colour. If you see this thin blue line leading from Vucitrn and then along the Gornja Sudimlja and Donja Sudimlja road and then moving on from Gornja Sudimlja, it should be the stream. Is it right to say that the stream is actually following the road from Gornja to Donja Sudimlja?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stream goes from Studime i Eperme to Vushtrri. I don't know in which river it flows.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: To Ceceli, yes, but that is immaterial now. Can you now tell me whether on this map -- can you see the letter G up there, that should be Gornja Sudimlja, and D marks Donja Sudimlja. Can you please now mark the location where you stopped around 4.00 p.m. on the 2nd of May?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Xhafa, do you know where Mahala Zvarca [phoen] or Mahala Zuci are? It should be somewhere in Donja Sudimlja. Do you know about those two locations?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now my question to you is: In your statement, in paragraph 5, the statement of 1989 [as interpreted], you say that after 4.00 p.m. no one was allowed to move because of a curfew, and in the transcript, Milosevic trial, page 4148, you said that: "After 4.00 p.m. we decided to take a rest in Sudimlja." Which one is correct then?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were ordered and we were told that after 4.00 p.m. it was a curfew in Vushtrri, so we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement you described that after 9.00 p.m., the police officers appeared. At that time it was already dark, right? You were still in the column of vehicles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Serb police and army came, we were sitting down on the field, and they ordered us all to go to our tractors, and ordered the drivers of the tractors to clear the road. Some people were walking, some people went and got on their tractors.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When you said "to clear the road," you mean to remove the tractors from the road not to have the column moved towards Vucitrn. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the tractors had to be removed from the middle of the road. It's in the direction towards Vushtrri. All the tractors had to line up on the right of the road in order for their vehicles to be able to pass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, it may just be me that has slightly lost his way a little. The statement you're referring to there is a statement we don't have. Is that correct? It was translated as "1989" -- well, by the translator I heard "1999," but I see it's appeared as 1989 on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction, this is statement 89(F).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, it's 89(F). Now, I -- it was translated as "1999" and I was trying to find it there, but it's now clear if it's the 89(F) statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, you told us - again, this is paragraph 5 - I don't that you hid Ismet in -- in the trailer after the incident that you had with the police. In fact, it was after the vehicles had been moved away from the road. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After everybody got on their tractors, a group of policemen came. I can't remember how many they were, whether there were three or four of them. They came to our tractor. They began to beat Ismet up. He was with Jetish on the tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we do have it in your statement. Thank you. I just want to ask you about some details. Please tell me, can you describe how you actually hid him in the trailer

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very easily. They left for a moment, so he came to the trailer and he laid down. We sat on him, and then we were trying to go on with our way but the next group of policemen came and they began to beat up Jetish.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We will get to that. But let me now ask you something about Ismet. At the Milosevic trial at page 4142 you stated that your brother's son was -- had been mobilised into the KLA and that he spent some time there and then returned home. And then on the same page you stated: All the young men had been mobilised at that time. Is that correct? Now, my question to you is in fact the following: Do you know anyone else who had been mobilised together with Ismet?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were not many of them that joined the KLA. There were young people that joined, of course, but I can't give you any names. Jetish responded to their mobilising order in the beginning, but then he came back home. He did not stay with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So let me go about this this way: Did you hear that in 1999 the KLA also had the mobilisation order put out?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, it was not like an order. It was voluntarily. Whoever wanted to join them, they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fine. And do you know whether anyone -- any other young men who had gone together with Ismet, whether they returned back home after their stay in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, your village, Donji Svracak, was it controlled by the KLA until the outbreak of the conflict with NATO on the 24th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no KLA in our village. In our village there were villagers who stayed there, and there were Serbs as well from our village who stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now, please tell me, there were no Serb police in your village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some villagers, Serb villagers, who had police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fine. I will now take you back to this location between Gornja Sudimlja and Donja Sudimlja, this is paragraph 6 of your 89(F) statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do that, Mr. Visnjic, this map we have on the screen which is marked, do you wish that copied at this stage or do you wish simply to leave it there in case you use it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, we can give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit IC21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, in paragraph 6 of your statement you describe how a second group of police officers came to your tractor. Now you call them paramilitaries. And in your statement you describe them, but what I want to ask you is whether perhaps they wore black masks over their faces?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The second group were not wearing masks, black masks. They had blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them had a vest, a green vest on, the one that beat Jetish.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did Jetish give him the money?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have any money left to give to the second group of policemen, so my sister-in-law gave him -- gave them some gold things that she had.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Who did she give it to?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policemen. She was somewhere in the middle of the tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In fact, she gave -- I apologise. Just a moment. So Hamide gave it, Fazil's wife. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Hamide, Fazli's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give us some estimate of the time that elapsed before the third group came? You said that around 10.30 -- the time is okay, but I would like to give us an estimate of the time that elapsed between the arrival of the second group and the third group. How much time elapsed, if you can recall at all?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: So when they took the jewellery and the gold, they left and we got off the tractor and started walking. I can't remember how long it took for the third group to come, and they came from behind a bush. Two of them were wearing masks. And they shot my brother. My father spoke something in Serbian. I don't know what he said, and they came back and took my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... statement, Mrs. Xhafa --

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about 10.30 after we decided to start walking. I can't remember exactly, but I remember that my brother said it was about -- it is 10.30 after the killing occurred.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was my brother's daughter who said it's 10.30.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me that you moved towards Vucitrn on foot before the third group arrived? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, after the killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fine. So when the third group appeared, was Jetish on the tractor?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Jetish was on the tractor. They took him. They shot him, they killed my father. After the killing, I can't tell you how long we were staying there shocked. We didn't know what to do, and the order came for us to move the tractor away. And they ordered a 13 year old to drive the tractor, but he was so young he couldn't drive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to that point. But we definitely will get to that point. I would like you to listen carefully to what I am asking you. I'm referring only to portions of your statement, specific portions. You don't have to go through it all again. I know that you want to tell the Court about it, but please focus on what I'm asking you. Now I would like to read out a sentence from paragraph 7 of your statement where you describe precisely this detail. In fact, it's several lines, but you say: "One of them," you are now referring to this group of policemen, "pointed a machine-gun at my mother's chest. Jetish had not had a chance to get back onto the tractor after being beaten when they took hold of him and dragged him to bush around 5 metres away on the right side." This is a sentence from paragraph 7 of your statement. From what I was able to gather on page 8, line 22 -- 21, in fact, you said that Jetish was on the tractor. So now I'm asking you, if you can recall at all, whether he was on the tractor or, as you described it here, he did not have a chance to get back onto the tractor after he was -- after he had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was close to the tractor. He wanted to get on the tractor. But we were discussing at that time whether to get off the tractor and walk or continue on the tractor. I don't know how long this lasted, and when we -- he was trying to get on the tractor, the third group -- this group of policemen came and they took Jetish and shot him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Were there any other people there at the place where Jetish was taken to, apart from himself and the police officers there by that bush?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a convoy of people, but at our tractor only the policemen came and Jetish, and there were four others close to the trailer. One of them put -- pointed the gun, the machine-gun, on my mother's chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So there were just the police officers and Jetish and no other people; for instance, no other tractor drivers. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Fine. Mrs. Xhafa, I put it to you that your brother Jetish was approached by two groups of paramilitaries not three, as you claim. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that misstates what's in her statement. She says "police officers," not "paramilitaries."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is irrelevant, in fact, but if, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be picked up as a positive confirmation that they were paramilitaries at a later stage when you're trolling through the transcript for your final submissions. So I think it ought to be put in a way that doesn't alter what she said so far. If you're challenging the identification of the personnel involved, you need to do that separately. And indeed, it's you who have called -- you have gone along with her description of them so far as police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, let me rephrase the question. I put it to you that your brother Jetish was approached by two, not three, groups of police, as you claim. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The correct thing is that three groups approached them. The first group beat up Ismet; the second group came, beat up Jetish, and asked for money; and the third group came and shot Jetish and our father.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, what I'm claiming is that Jetish -- that it was Jetish and not Hamide who gave all the money in their possession. So Jetish gave them the money, not Hamide, as you claim. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked money from Jetish and from my father. They went to my father to ask for money while they were beating up Jetish. And my sister-in-law, because she knew he had no money, she gave all her valuables, jewellery and gold, and then they left when they took it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, it is still my position that the second group of policemen again asked for money and that Jetish had nothing left to give. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Jetish did not have anything to give them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, I put it to you that Jetish was told to go to where the bushes were, together with a few other tractor drivers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. He was close to the tractor -- the bush was close to the tractor. They took him to that bush. It was right in front of us that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, I also put it to you that at the moment when he was ordered to go to the shrub together with the other few tractor drivers and that he was shot at when he caught up with that group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about other drivers. I'm speaking here about Jetish and my family. They took Jetish only to that bush. When they took Jetish, these people in masks, they didn't exchange any words. They just pointed the gun at him. I know that my father said something, and they also took my father and they shot him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question at page 10, line 7, through to page 12, line 4, these questions are based on paragraph 6 of the statement given by Jetish Xhafa to the OTP investigators on the 26th of February, 2000, at page K0075428.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, you say that - this was in paragraph 8 of your 89(F) statement - you say you heard three shots when your father was being shot at. In that paragraph, as regards the third shot, you said: "I heard another shot, but I didn't see where it came from." Could you clarify it for us, please?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they took my father, we realised that he would be killed as well. We heard a shot and then another. I turned my head around because I didn't want to look. I heard a cry, and they both remained killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you hear the third shot after that? Because this is the way I read your statement, if I understand it correctly.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many shots. The police were shooting all the time. There were other tractors around, where there were shots as well, from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you are stating that there was general firing in your environs and that the police fired on several occasions and many shots. Did I understand your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because when we started to walk, we passed some corpses on the road; that means that other people were killed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, it was quite dark at that time of day and you didn't see -- well, how far ahead or behind you were you able to see, having in mind the time of day?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a clear night. The moon was shining, and the tractors had their lights on. So we could see very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Your uncle, Muharrem, was he with you in the column perhaps?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. But we met him on the way to Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You met him later as well then?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your statement you continue to describe how you were ordered to set the tractors in motion and that only Lavdim knew how to drive a tractor, how to operate it. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ismet was there as well, but because he was hiding and we didn't dare ask him, "Drive the tractor," for fear of being caught, we didn't know what to do. A Serb came and asked him to start the tractor. He just could drive it for a hundred metres, no more, and we stopped then and we continued on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And then Ismet abandoned you, he left. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the tractor stopped and we started to walk, we looked around. There were no policemen. We got off the tractor. Ismet was with us in the group, and we walked together until we joined another group. And there was a time when the police left, so he took the chance and went on the other side of the road and went towards Samodreza to meet the KLA, and he met them after that one day or two, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And did you see Ismet again?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war ended, we met Ismet. I think it was on the 17th of June. I went to see my brother and I met Ismet as well in Samodreza.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did the -- the KLA escort the convoy for a while? If they were moving towards Dreza, they must have accompanied you at least part of the way?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. When we joined the convoy from Sllakovc, the KLA went in a different direction. We did not see the KLA or meet them that day. There were only unarmed people, civilians, in the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In what direction did the KLA go; do you know?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was in the opposite direction. Maybe towards Llapi.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Weren't the Serbian forces coming from the other direction? They were advancing, and that was one of the reasons why you went towards Vucitrn?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The opposite direction is towards Dumnica, and from there they went towards the villages of Llapi. I don't know. While the Serbian forces came from the direction of Sekovc --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Vesekovc, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When you say "Dumnica," is it the location --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I will have to ask again for 3D66 to be put in front of the witness so that she can indicate where the location is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When you say "Dumnica," is it the place we see on the map to the right-hand side of Samodreza?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dumnica is somewhere here, upper Dumnica. I didn't ask or know where they were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you partially followed the road between Sllakovc to Samodreza, and then you turned towards Gornja Sudimlja. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mrs. Xhafa. I wanted to ask you the following. In paragraph 11 of your 89(F) statement, you state that while in Vucitrn your uncle Muharrem went to see a Serb by the name of Biba who was your neighbour, and he explained to him your situation, and then he helped get Jetish's sons released. My question is, therefore, this man, this Biba, was he a policeman?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So what did Muharrem explained to him, what situation, that your father and probably your brother were killed that night. Is that what he told him?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he told him the truth, everything that had happened to us that night. I don't know how much he helped us, but that day our sons were not taken to prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And this was all on the 3rd of May, 1999, before noon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And your uncle basically reported the murders of your brother and your father, although at that time you didn't know that your brother -- whether your brother had survived. So your uncle reported your father's and your brother's murders to the policemen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the police took any steps after that?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted to ask you this, Mrs. Xhafa, from the same paragraph: In the territory of the Vucitrn municipality, were there some people with tractors who stayed behind and didn't leave towards Albania? Because in your statement you state that all those who had tractors went to Albania. I'm asking you now: Do you know whether -- of anyone who had a tractor and who remained instead of going to Albania?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know? As far as I know, all the tractors were ordered to go to Albania. The people left on foot, were asked to go to the Kicic and Smrekonice.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you don't really know whether all those who had tractors were ordered indeed to go to Albania?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: While you were in the village of Dobra Luka, there you describe an event in paragraph 15 of your statement, where you say that you saw the Serb police go to one part of Dobra Luka. And then you said you heard some shots and that you were around 200 metres away from that place. You don't really know whether they took away those Albanian families, including women and children. You didn't see that. Is that correct

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see, but I could hear the shooting and we could see them enter that neighbourhood on that day. The following day, we learned that they had taken the children and women and the remaining men there in the direction of the villages Stutarice [phoen], Okrashtica, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Xhafa.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This concludes my cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Visnjic. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. By your leave, before I start posing questions, I wanted to address the problem I discussed with Mr. Hannis. This refers to the patterns on camouflage uniforms, and this refers to this and the next witness. Unfortunately, none of us can make out what exactly is in the pictures, in the photographs. I discussed this issue with my learned friend Mr. Hannis, and I understand their situation. I just wanted to point out this problem because it will have to do with both this witness and the next witness, who is also going to be invited to recognise the patterns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, as I see it, the Prosecution have failed to give us copies of these uniforms that are capable of being identified, and that therefore the evidence at the moment lacks any specification so far as it relates to these pictures. So the only way you can deal with it, I think, is to try to describe things to the witness and cross-examine on the basis that these don't exist. And it may be that later will be too late for the Prosecution to introduce them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will have a few short questions, by your leave, for Mrs. Xhafa. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Xhafa, good morning. My name is Djuro Cepic, attorney-at-law, and I appear here on behalf of General Vladimir Lazarevic as a member of the Defence. Today you stated that together with the police -- you've described that the convoy was approached by the military as well, but as you stated the military were somewhere in the middle or at the rear of the convoy, whereas you yourself were at the front. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were somewhere in the middle of the convoy, in the middle part, while the military and -- moved along the convoy in their military vehicles. Some were at the entrance of Studime i Ulet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you. I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: They were moving in the opposite direction of where you were going?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They went up to the upper part and then came down with their vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. I apologise. [In English] I do apologise, I will withdraw my intention that I -- I've got some additional questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood your statement well, when you said they were at the rear of the column, they were not close to you. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were resting there at the entrance of Studime i Ulet, there was a tank, a military tank. And those who manned that tank made us shout: Draza, Draza, Sloba, Sloba.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You didn't mention that in your statement. In fact, you said something quite the opposite.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I said the opposite. This is the truth, what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In English, page 2, paragraph 5; in Albanian, paragraph 2, page 3, you said: "Members of paramilitary units approached our tractors on several occasions." Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you couldn't clearly make out the insignia they wore as -- on the members of, as you put it, the military. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The previous soldiers you mentioned, not the paramilitaries. The soldiers. You couldn't see -- make out their insignia when they moved in the -- along in those vehicles. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could see the tank, but not the insignia, no. And we didn't dare look at that direction and see what kind of insignia they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, what's the significance of the chant: Draza, Draza?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a Chetnik gang, a Serbian Chetnik gang from the past, and they made us chant the name, his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Xhafa. My name is Branko Lukic. Together with Mr. Ivetic and Mr. Ogrizovic, I represent Mr. Lukic as his Defence counsel. I will have a few questions related to your statements tendered by the Prosecution in this case, and now I would like you to answer as briefly as possible so that we are able to complete this as soon as possible. And if the Judges or the Prosecutors think that you need to provide any further explanation, they will, I'm sure, ask for those explanations. In paragraph 2 of your 89(F) statement of the 25th of August, 2006, you say that you were forced to leave your house because Serbs started burning houses in your village. In your statement of 11th of October, 2001, the English version that's page 2, paragraph 2; Albanian version, again page 2, paragraph 2; and in Serbian it is page 2, paragraph 3, you say: "We moved out of the village because some of our neighbours, Serbs, from the same village moved out and went to the village of Nedakovc. We thought that something would happen and we decided to go." Now, in relation to this part of your statement, let me ask the you the following question. How many Serb households were there in your village?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the Serb families moved out of your village before you, yourself, left your village?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. They left a day before we did. They went to the village of Nedakovc. Our Albanian neighbours who were there, they came with us, and they actually informed us that all the Serbs left the village. We saw that the houses were set on fire in Sfracak e Eperm; therefore, we decided to leave as well and set off in the direction of Studime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the houses were set on fire one day before you left the village?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, on that day while the Serbs left the village, a day before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So on the day when the Serbs left the village, which is one day before you left the village, the houses were on fire?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The houses were set on fire on the day we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you moved out of your village, you headed towards the villages that were much stronger strongholds of the KLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we thought that there won't be Serbs in that zone and felt it would be safer for us to go to Dumnice, while the KLA was in Sllakovc. And from Dumnice then we went to Sllakovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did this arrangement come about for you to leave the village? How was this agreement reached? Did anyone order you to leave?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We could see the danger coming towards us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Madam, Mrs. Xhafa, is it not correct that the departure from your village was in fact organised by the KLA? In fact, they helped you pack?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. We left ourselves. There was no KLA in our village, and the KLA was very far from our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today you were asked whether the area in which your village was, whether it was in fact controlled by the KLA. You also said that there was no police in this area, just the locals, Serbs as you put it, who had police uniforms. Those inhabitants of your village, did they have the regular police uniforms or were their uniforms different from those of the regular police?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had police uniforms. And we could see them even earlier dressed in these uniforms, in blue police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of weapons they had?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that the uniforms possibly worn by the people in the villages, and those people in fact were members of the local security, that those uniforms differed from the uniforms worn by the regular police, would you allow that this was in fact possible?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. It's not a problem. I will repeat my question. If I were to tell you -- if I were to claim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess I'm objecting for a lack of foundation. I don't know that we've established with this witness what a regular police uniform looks like to compare it to anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's an unanswerable question as phrased at the moment. I think the witness's statement was quite right. Now, I assume that it was going to be clarified, so let's hear what the alternative question is, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. I thought you were asking me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no. Let's hear what Mr. Lukic's alternative version is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, it would be much easier if we had the pictures that you used in the identification process to determine what uniforms in fact you were able to identify. Unfortunately, we don't have this picture, and as instructed by the Chamber we have to go about it this way. That is why I have to apologise if I have to dwell on this for a little while longer, but we will have to do that in order to determine some things that we can't determine in any other way. My question is as follows: Would you agree with my claim and would you allow that it is possible that the uniforms worn by the people in your village were, in fact, different from the uniforms worn by the regular police?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have the same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's the same question. It's impossible to -- to know whether the witness can answer that because we have no idea what her experience of regular police uniforms is. So, as Mr. Hannis points out, we don't have a foundation for the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't -- I don't know if it would be of any assistance to counsel or not. We have Exhibit P2254 which has photos of various military and police uniforms. Now, if Mr. Lukic has seen that and any of those meet his definition of what a regular police uniform is, maybe he would like to show it to her and inquire if she recognises any of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a helpful suggestion, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I haven't been using that evidence in preparation for this witness, so I might try --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I perhaps try to understand the significance of the question. If you accept that there are police -- or there are Serbs in the village who wear what she describes as police uniforms, what's the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The issue is that it is not -- it's not the police force, it's a local security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but that's not going to be determined by her knowledge of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I tried --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Her identification of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe she knew. I don't know. I tried to -- maybe it was a bit of fishing expedition, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you're saying that they are not under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, is that going to be -- is that particular point going to be determined by looking at pictures of uniform?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It doesn't seem to me it's going to advance our knowledge of the matter, so it might be better if you proceed to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Xhafa, the KLA strongholds were located in Studime i Eperme and Ceceli, and your column was heading precisely in that direction. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 you describe the size of the column and you say that there were around 50.000 people in it. When asked by my colleague Visnjic, you say that you were sure that there were no KLA members in the column. Did you know each and every one of the 50.000 people in the column?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know them, but I'm sure that there were no KLA soldiers in the convoy. The army left in the opposite direction, and the convoy was void of KLA members. These were all civilians from Llap-Shala area, some were from Vushtrri. It was a large number of people in that convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that KLA members often threw down their weapons and removed their uniforms and joined the civilians?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that KLA members, while they were in their villages, often moved about in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I didn't go out to investigate who was wearing what kind of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what my point is, Mrs. Xhafa. For you, only a person in a uniform is a member of the KLA. Is that correct? Or let me try and rephrase my question. If there were some KLA members in the column wearing civilian clothes, would you be able to recognise that person as a KLA member?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I would because I would recognise the KLA uniform. But as I said, there were no KLA members, soldiers, in uniforms in the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be enough. I would now like to move on to paragraph 5 of your statement; our Defence believes that it is one of the most contentious parts. And in this respect I would like to ask you: My learned colleague Mr. Visnjic discussed with you the issue of how many times your column -- or in fact, your tractor was approached by members of various formations. Mrs. Xhafa, to what extent are you in fact able to distinguish among members of the military, police, paramilitaries, local security? Because I would like to ask you a few questions about that. So my first question to you is: Are you sure when you categorise a certain group of people as belonging to a certain formation, are you sure about what formation a certain group belongs to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what do you have in mind, Mr. Lukic? You need to give her a specific example, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can go to specifics, but I try to elicit from this witness whether she's really sure about what she is claiming in this statement or not. And I will go to the specifics, yes. Or you want me to start --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think it's a pretty useless question to ask her whether she's sure about whether people belong to certain formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps her degree of certainty is different depending on the circumstances. We really need to look at the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Xhafa, as instructed by the Trial Chamber, let me now ask you a specific question. In your previous statements, not the 89(F) statement, the statement from the 26th of February, 2000, the second group, the group consisting of four police officers, in English version that would be the last paragraph in page 2; Albanian version, page 2, second -- page 3, paragraph 2, you say about this group that they were paramilitaries. In this statement you say: "At around 9.00 p.m. four Serb police officers arrived. They were shooting in the air with their machine-guns." That is why I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification, Your Honour. I believe she referred to this as the first group to approach them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I -- now that we're jumping between statements, of course it's difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's try this the first group, actually. Yes, I'm sorry. It's paragraph 5, Your Honour, of the 89(F) statement. It's fourth sentence or fifth sentence in that paragraph. It says: [Interpretation] "We were surrounded on all sides by Serb military. Around 9.00 p.m. four policemen arrived. They were shooting in the air with their machine-guns." In the previous statement, the four men were described as four paramilitaries. Now I would like to ask a question that would allow the witness to explain why at one time she thought that these men had been paramilitaries and at another time she thought these men had been police officers. Whatever the explanation can be provided by the witness as to what details made her --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, Mrs. Xhafa, what are the details that made you change your statement and your mind so that now you think that these people are -- were in fact police, not the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not clear to me to which group you are referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first group, the four men who approached your tractor. You have it in paragraph 5 of your 89(F) statement, if you have it in front of you.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I help you with it. You have the statement in front of you, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It appears she has her 89(F) statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. And if you look at paragraph 5 of that statement --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- you will see just around the middle of the statement: "Around 9.00 p.m. four Serb policemen arrived."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, when you made a statement in February 2000 to the Office of the Prosecution, you described these four people as four paramilitaries. The question you're being asked is: Why are the two statements different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To me, "paramilitaries" are those who wear police uniforms, black gloves, masks, and that's why I call them "paramilitaries."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude then that when you gave the first statement in February 2000, that you recalled -- remembered these people as people wearing police uniforms, black masks, and black gloves? And now, when you gave this statement in August this year, you no longer remembered that group in the same way; in other words, dressed in the same way. Can you now explain to us how this difference between the two statements came about?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already answered this question. In the beginning, the group that I described with the gloves was described as paramilitaries, and I told you already why I called them paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've drawn from the answer, Mr. Lukic, the exact opposite impression from the one I've drawn. The witness is saying that they are the same, and she's using two different words to describe the same people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, but then we have the next question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- the next sentence actually, the second one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which one, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The third sentence -- fourth sentence, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say: "Members of the paramilitaries were shouting at the tractor drivers to clear the road for their armoured vehicles to be able to pass." So all around you were the people that you describe as wearing black gloves, masks, and they are in your vicinity and they are actually shouting at the tractor drivers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were walking beside the column and they were shouting at the drivers of tractors and they were shooting in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You go on to say that they were cursing and insulting you in Serbian. You don't speak Serbian, Mrs. Xhafa. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you able to read Serbian?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you able to read Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, it is impossible to be able to read something a little bit. Either you know all the letters or you don't.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, yes. I might have even forgotten a letter or two in Cyrillic, but I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Xhafa. It is now time for our break, if the Trial Chamber agrees with me that this is the right time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Can you indicate how long roughly you'll be?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a few issues to clarify with this witness, so I hope that I can finish in one hour. I'll try my best to cut it short as much as possible, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, I will try to put concise questions to you. In any case, I'll try to be more concise and precise than before the break, and I would kindly ask for similar answers provided to you [as interpreted], so that we can try to finish this as soon as possible, and I also realise that the Trial Chamber was not all too pleased to hear that I would have another hour of questions. Today in the transcript, which is page 4, line 22, you mentioned some paramilitaries shouting at tractor drivers to clear the road so that they could pass with their vehicles. Did those vehicles pass indeed?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In what direction did they go?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning they went in the direction of Vushtrri, and then they came back from Vushtrri down. So they went up and down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What sort of vehicles were there?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact answer here because I did not look very closely to those vehicles, but they were military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you posed that question on the basis that she said a group of paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Had told her that move. Now, the words that are on the English transcript are "police." That's page 4 from this morning you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. But in her statement, paragraph 5, it says: [Interpretation] "Members of paramilitary units were shouting at tractor drivers to clear the road so that their armoured vehicles could pass through."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but look at your question. Your question is: Today in the transcript you mentioned some paramilitaries shouting at tractor drivers ... Now, that's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it takes us back to the problem we had just before the break, on which perhaps some further clarification is required.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, you remember I pointed out to you that in your two statements you described the four Serb persons who came towards you as a -- differently. On one statement you described them as police and in the other you described them as paramilitaries. Now, what we would like to be clear about is: Have you changed your description of these people? You previously called them paramilitaries. In the statement you did recently for this case, you called them police. Is that a different description? In other words, are you thinking of different people from what you were thinking -- or from the people you were thinking of when you made the original statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There were policemen in blue uniforms. There were others with black gloves, and this group wearing black gloves, this is the group that I called paramilitaries. And this was my answer before as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the four people who you say: "Around 9.00 p.m. four," and you say now, "Serb policemen arrived." Now, what were these four people wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had blue uniforms -- but there were others along the road who had black gloves. There were many others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let me read what the statement says a bit further. It says: "Around 9.00 p.m. four Serb policemen arrived. They were shooting in the air with their machine-guns. They were cursing and shouting insults at us in Serbian."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, what were these four people wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And they didn't have the masks or the black gloves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, others had the gloves. They were circulating along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, in the same statement, the next sentence reads: "Members of paramilitaries shouted at tractor drivers to clear the road so that their vehicles could move along." That is why I asked you about those vehicles. Did you see who operated those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I know? I did not have a look who was driving those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you don't know whether those vehicles belonged to the people who were shouting at you?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were shouting were on foot, they were walking, and these vehicles were other vehicles. I think they belonged to the army. That's why we had to clear the road for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to move on to paragraph 7 of your statement. In the second sentence of the paragraph you state: "Two were wearing black Balaclava masks with holes for the eyes and mouth. They had blue camouflage uniforms." Is this the description you provided for the members of paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the people in black masks were paramilitaries, yes. I don't know what kind of police that would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And those are the people who shot Jetish and your father. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the moment when the masked people took Jetish away, you mentioned there was some shooting at the same time close to or around where you were. Did you know that at that moment there was fighting between the KLA and the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. There was no fighting between the KLA and the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were on the tractor - and we know it was around 10.30 p.m. - in what direction did these masked people take Jetish in relation to where you were, in front of you, to your black, to your left, to your right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They killed Jetish in front of us [as interpreted]. They got him off on the right side. It was right in front of our eyes that he was killed. We were on the tractor trailer when it happened, and I could see everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that related to this incident there was a police patrol who was sent out to carry out an on-site investigation relating to the murders, but they were forced to return as they were attacked by the KLA? And that was two days after the conflict in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if there's a document relating to this which the cross-examination is done, I haven't received it from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How did you expect the witness to know the answer to this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If she knows; if she does not, she will tell me. And we'll use a document in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know anything of this, Ms. Xhafa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know anything about this conflict with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know, Mrs. Xhafa, that two days after the fighting the KLA again seized control of the very same territory?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I know that on the 4th of May the bodies were collected by the civilians, and they were buried in Studime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What civilians, Mrs. Xhafa?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who remained there that night in Studime. There were civilians. People from Sllakovc and other villages came and helped bury the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you testifying now that not everyone left with the column of refugees?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people there that night hiding in the mountains, and those people helped bury the bodies. And also people from other villages who had heard about the event, the incident, came to help as well. I think there were about 115 people who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were those people from the neighbouring villages? Did they help with the burial of those killed?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they buried them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, just hold on, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Just going back to page 35 of the transcript, line 10, the question ends: "Paramilitary units." Then I believe the answer begins, but it's not indicated that that's part of the answer. Page 35, line 10. "I think" I believe is the first part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that, Mr. O'Sullivan. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, to go back to the topic. Therefore, there were resident civilians in the nearby villages who hadn't left with the column of refugees that you've described for us, and those civilians helped bury the killed people?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told you earlier that there were people in hiding that night, they were hiding in the mountains. There were people from Studime i Eperme and -- who had returned to their own homes. And on the 4th of May they came back and helped bury the dead. Other people came from Dumnica, Cecelija, I don't know where from. So they came to Studime to help bury the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the area controlled by the Serbian forces when those civilians came in?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wanted to tell you who was with those civilians. The KLA was there, and you yourself said they remained in that area, that they hadn't left with the rest of you. Isn't it true that the KLA remained in the area you left from?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I already said that there were people who were hiding, and days later the KLA helped them bury the dead. The funeral service was on the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I was asking, Mrs. Xhafa. You can see for yourself that now we come to the point that indeed the KLA was present in the region one or two days after the fighting. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came to bury the dead when they realised that there had been people who had been killed in Studime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will take this as an affirmative answer to my question whether there was the KLA there. If I'm mistaken, please correct me, but I wanted to move on.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA came on the day of the burial. I don't know how else to explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the moment of KLA entry, there were no Serbian forces in their area. Isn't that correct? Or did you hear of any fighting on the day of the funeral or the burial?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything about any fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, at that moment and in that region there were no more Serbian forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this. I don't know how to respond to this question. I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will rephrase, put it another way. Were there any Serbian forces present at the time of burial?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not present at the cemetery. Maybe they were further away, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is my assertion that they were further away. In fact, so far away that they no longer controlled the area on the day of the burial. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 9, you talk about sending Ismet to notify KLA fighters who were in the mountains about what had happened. Is it true that you knew where the KLA units were?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ismet left that night. He stayed at a mountain called Gradina, and I believe he thought he would meet the KLA soldiers there. I don't know whether it was the next day or the day after that where -- when he met some soldiers in Dumnica, and he joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he join their ranks after having met them?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He joined the soldiers the next day or the day after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Some of your family members were, therefore, members of the KLA. Did they wear KLA uniforms all the time?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No member of my family was in the KLA. The only one was Ismet. As I said, he withdrew. But on the 2nd of May, as I said, he went to the KLA headquarters and he stayed with them until the war ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Xhafa. I think we've clarified that sufficiently. I wanted to ask you something about paragraph 13. There you speak about a small blue cardboard box -- oh, actually, it's a -- it was a card. You said you were required to register and your name was put on that, and it used as a permit to be able to stay in one of the houses in Dobra Luka. Did you know that, say, the Serbs who had come from Kosovo to Serbia had to undergo the same procedure, that they were given the same blue card? It is the regular procedure of reporting a place of residence. You are familiar with that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't -- I didn't have any contact with Serbs to discuss with them whether they had such cards or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same paragraph you also state that: "Later in the hospital yard one of the policemen whom I recognised as Deputy Commander Simic ordered us to go back to our houses and not to assist the KLA in any way." For example, including providing food supplies. Did you return to your houses after that?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we returned to our homes where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it an order or did the man simply tell you: You may go to your houses now?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an order. We were told to go home, not to help the KLA. If they would see any KLA member in Dobra Luka, then everybody would be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the police in fact carried out investigations and interrogations to try and establish who was a member of the KLA? It wasn't killing anyone they thought was a member of the KLA. Didn't you say yourself that they took people to the prison in Smrekovnica and then after, those same people were released after questioning. Is it correct that the police carried out investigations and interrogations relating to possible membership in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not everybody was a member of the KLA. All the people who were imprisoned were civilians and they kept them there. Some of them were sent to Albania, while others, their bodies have been returned from Serbia very recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony today that some of the people who were taken to Smrekovnica were killed?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was any of your family killed in the prison in Smrekovnica?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Other people. I've heard that some bodies have been returned from Serbia recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You never mentioned this before. It is not found in any of your statements. You are now stating that someone was killed among the people who had been taken to Smrekovnica.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody knew what was happening with the people who were sent to the prison in Smrekovnica. I only learned about my family members, and this I learned very late, that they were sent to Albania. But members of the families of people who had been in Smrekovnica have told me that their bodies were returned from Serbia later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us a name so that we can try and verify what you're stating. Who told you and for which family member who was in the prison in Smrekovnica that they were killed?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dritan Merovci, his body was returned recently. It was found in Serbia. I can't remember any other names now. But there were many other people, the bodies of whom were returned recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know how the man you mentioned was killed?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was killed in the Smrekovnica prison?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was killed. I know that he was taken to that prison, but his body was returned from Serbia one -- a year earlier, a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had been released from the Smrekovnica prison or is it something you don't know?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He came from Serbia as a dead body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 15 of your statement: "One morning in May 1999, around 8.00 a.m., I was at a house where we were staying when I saw the Serb police go to one quarter of Dobra Luka. These police were wearing green camouflage uniforms but they were too far away from me for me to make out any insignia on their uniforms." Well, what's led you to conclude that the men in green camouflage uniforms were police?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how I would otherwise have described them. They were quite a ways away, and I couldn't really distinguish them well. I don't really know whether they were police or army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Xhafa. In paragraph 16 you say: "I later heard" - so you don't have any direct of that. This is something that you heard about - "from some people ... from Donja Sudimlja, "from Jashar Rashica and Emine Rashica that they had been made to stand in front of Serb tanks on the front line and that the police separated ten people from the group." Did the Serb police have tanks, Mrs. Xhafa, do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people Jashar Rashica and Emine Rashica were in that neighbourhood. And when Emine returned, they -- she was shot at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Xhafa, the question is a very specific one. Do you know whether the Serb police - the question is confined to police - did have tanks as part of their normal equipment? That's the question that's being asked. And if you don't know the answer to that, just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I just wanted to explain something that had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, we already have the account of what happened in writing, it's just certain particular points that need to be clarified. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this: Would you agree with my suggestion that the Serb police did not have any tanks and that no police officers are in fact able to drive a tank? So would you agree with if I were to put that to you, would you agree that this was a very probable statement?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were police on foot who drove the people out of their homes, but there were other people who were driving tanks and they lined them up in front of the tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And thank you, Mrs. Xhafa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've tried to cut -- make this as short as possible, so I don't have any further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do have some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, first of all, I want one more time to try to go through the chronology of the men who approached your tractor and your family on the 2nd of May. In your statement in paragraph 5, you were talking about 9.00 p.m., there were four Serbs who approached. What uniforms were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had blue camouflaged uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did any of these four have the black mask or the gloves that you spoke of before?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The four near the tractor, no; but there were others a ways away who had black masks and gloves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Then what you referred to in your statement at paragraph 6 is the second group who approached, and this included the fat man with the stick who beat Jetish. You describe in your statement that they were wearing the blue camouflage uniforms. Did any of this group have the gloves or the mask?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The person who beat Jetish had a green camouflage jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In your statement you describe that as a vest. The translation now came across as a jacket. Did it have sleeves or not, the green piece of clothing?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, without -- without sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
